analysis.investment_thesis: Rikhav Securities rides India's retail financialization tailwind with a cheap 6.6x P/E and healthy 64% promoter holding, but margin collapse in FY25 (net profit fell from ₹42cr to ₹24cr despite revenue tripling to ₹328cr) and deeply negative ₹188cr OCF signal operating fragility in a cyclical broking business. Wait for proof that the scale-up is profitable before committing conviction capital.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR 108.9% (FY22→FY25) riding India's demat/retail broking boom
Promoter holding a solid 64.06% with low borrowings (₹5cr) and equity nearly tripling to ₹244cr
Cheap headline valuation at P/E 6.63, ROCE 16.7%
key_risks: Net profit fell 43% in FY25 (₹42cr→₹24cr) while revenue tripled — severe margin compression
OCF positive only 1 of last 4 years; FY25 OCF of -₹188cr raises working-capital/client-funds concerns
Broking is hyper-cyclical; ROE 12.9% is below my 15% threshold and will crater in a bear market
red_flags: Operating margin collapse: EBITDA stagnant (₹56cr→₹35cr) despite revenue tripling
Small-cap broker with recent BSE listing — limited public track record through a down cycle
analysis.detailed_analysis:
India's stockbroking sector is a structural winner — demat accounts have multiplied, SIPs cross ₹25,000cr/month, and retail participation is still underpenetrated. Rikhav ticks the surface boxes: 30-year vintage, 64% promoter skin-in-the-game, near-zero debt, and a P/E of 6.6x that looks like a bargain. The revenue ramp from ₹36cr to ₹328cr in three years is eye-catching and suggests the company is capturing this tailwind.

But the numbers beneath don't add up the way I'd want. When revenue triples and net profit halves, something is structurally wrong — either they're booking low-margin principal/arbitrage volumes, or cost structure ballooned faster than franchise value. FY25 OCF of -₹188cr is enormous for a ₹159cr market cap company, even accounting for client-fund movements typical of brokers. Compare this to Motilal Oswal, 5paisa, or Angel One — the cleaner compounders — and Rikhav looks like a less-proven, more-volatile bet. I'd watch 2-3 quarters for margin stabilization and positive OCF before taking a position; the India broking thesis is real, but the right jockey matters more than a cheap ticket.
